paper.title: Semi Bandit Dynamics in Congestion Games: Convergence to Nash Equilibrium and No-Regret Guarantees

unmapped: Costs are non-negative and bounded by c_max (c^t_e in [0, c_max]), not normalized to [0,1]
Strategy set is a family of subsets of m resources given implicitly via the H-representation {x in [0,1]^m : A x <= b} of its convex hull
settings.definition_quote: Agent $i$ selects a prob. distribution $\pi_i^t \in \Delta(\mathcal{P}_i)$. An adversary selects a cost function $c^t: E \mapsto \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$. Agent $i$ samples a path $p^t_i \sim \pi_i^t$ and suffers cost $C_i(p^t_i, c^t) := \sum_{e \in p_i^t} c_e^t$. Agent $i$ learns the costs $c_e^t$ for all resources $e \in p_i^t$

settings.name_in_paper: Semi-Bandit Game Dynamics in congestion games (convergence to Nash Equilibrium)
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Game-theoretic convergence of all n agents to an approximate mixed Nash equilibrium in a congestion game, not a single-learner bandit regret guarantee
unmapped: n selfish agents in a congestion game with m resources, non-decreasing resource cost functions bounded by c_max
Objective: time-averaged exploitability (best-iterate convergence to epsilon-approximate mixed NE)
settings.definition_quote: Each agent $i \in [n]$ (randomly) selects a strategy $p^t_i \in \mathcal{P}_i$ and suffers cost ... Each agent $i \in [n]$ \textbf{learns only} the congestion costs $c_e(p_i^t,p^t_{-i})$ of her selected resources $e \in p_i^t$.

algorithms.name: Semi-Bandit Gradient Descent with Caratheodory Exploration (SBGD-CE / OGD-CE, Algorithm 2)

symbols.c_max: upper bound on resource costs, ||c^t||_inf <= c_max

source.label: t:regret
source.quote: Let $p_i^1,\ldots,p^T_i \in \mathcal{P}_i$ the sequence of strategies produced by Algorithm~\ref{alg:alg1} given as input the costs $c^1,\ldots,c^T$ with $\norm{c^t}_\infty \leq c_{\max}$. Then with probability $1- \delta$, \[\sum_{t=1}^T\sum_{e \in p^t_i} c_e^t - \min_{p_i^\star \in \mathcal{P}_i}\sum_{e \in p^\star_i} c_e^t \leq \mathcal{O}\left(mc^2_{\max}T^{4/5} \log(1/\delta) \right)\]

results.notes: Realized regret against best fixed strategy w.p. 1-delta. Remark 3.6 states that choosing delta = O(1/(m T c_max)) gives Õ(m^2 c_max^2 T^{4/5}) regret (the paper's headline O(m^2 T^{4/5})). Step sizes do not depend on T, so anytime. Note the proof's final expression has a m^2 T^{3/5} and T^{1/5}*sqrt(T) terms; the stated order is as printed.

source.label: remarkT34
source.quote: The better $\mathcal{O}(m^{3/2}T^{3/4})$ regret bound can be obtained by selecting the parameters $\gamma_t = c_{\max}^{-1}m^{-1/2}t^{-3/4}$ and $\mu_t = \min(1/m_i, m^{-1/2}t^{-1/4})$. However such a parameter selection leads to $\mathcal{O}(T^{-1/8})$ convergence rate to NE.

results.notes: Stated in a remark without proof; probability type (high-probability vs expectation) and c_max dependence not specified; 'expectation' field is a placeholder since regret type unspecified.

source.label: thm:convergence_to_nash
source.quote: Let $\pi^1,\ldots, \pi^T$ the sequence of strategy profiles produced if all agents adopt Algorithm~\ref{alg:alg1}. Then for all $T \geq \Theta\left( m^{12.5}n^{7.5}/\epsilon^5 \right)$, \[\frac{1}{T}\E \left[\sum_{t=1}^T\max_{i \in [n]}\left[c_i(\pi^{t}_i, \pi^{t}_{-i}) - \min_{\pi_i \in \Delta(\mathcal{P}_i)} c_i(\pi_i, \pi_{-i}^{t})\right]\right] \leq \epsilon.\]

results.notes: Number of rounds sufficient for time-averaged expected exploitability <= epsilon (best-iterate convergence to epsilon-mixed NE). N = number of agents n. Corollary c:markov converts this into high-probability statements via Markov's inequality.

source.label: thm:convergence_to_nash
source.quote: The same holds for $T \geq \Theta(n^{6.5}m^{7}/\epsilon^5)$ in case the agents know $n,m$ and select $\gamma_t :=\Theta(m^{-4/5} n^{-8/5}c^{-1}_{\max} t^{-3/5})$ and $\mu_t := \Theta(n^{-6/5}m^{-11/10} t^{-1/5})$.

results.notes: Second case of the same theorem: tuned parameters requiring knowledge of n, m, c_max. Proof bound has a log T factor neglected in the statement.
